subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw add a native masked-secrets/process-isolation boundary for agent-executed commands, extend plugin or CredentialProvider seams instead, or keep this outside core as OS/plugin isolation guidance?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the durable fix defines a credential trust boundary and config/API surface rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor security-owned native design
options.body: Define a core credential-isolation boundary with dispatch-time injection, exact redaction, migration/docs, and plugin-provider integration before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin/CredentialProvider seams
options.body: Keep core lean and prioritize the missing plugin or credential-provider APIs needed for packages such as credential-vault to cover this safely.

options.title: Close as external hardening only
options.body: Treat OS user isolation, external proxies, and ClawHub plugins as the supported path, and explicitly decline a core masked-secrets surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor security-owned native design
recommendation.body: Define a core credential-isolation boundary with dispatch-time injection, exact redaction, migration/docs, and plugin-provider integration before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The question is a security-boundary decision on paths CODEOWNERS routes to the security owner group.
